analysis.body:
# Grid Interconnection Snapshot: September 2026

Across the five major US grid operators, nearly 1.3 million megawatts of planned generation and storage sits in interconnection queues—ERCOT alone holds 438,086 MW across 1,778 projects, with MISO following at 299,721 MW from 3,846 requests. This backlog represents roughly 18 months of work at historical interconnection speeds. Storage capacity queued totals roughly 326,000 MW when summing ERCOT, MISO, SPP, and CAISO—a signal that data center operators and their utilities expect sustained power demand growth, since battery storage is primarily deployed to smooth loads rather than to replace generation.

Gas-fired generation in these queues totals about 184,345 MW across the five operators, representing just 14 percent of total queued capacity but suggesting that natural gas will remain a bridging fuel during transition periods. Solar leads by fuel type at roughly 428,764 MW queued, reflecting both falling costs and manufacturing capacity, while wind adds another 169,742 MW. The concentration of projects in Texas (438,086 MW in ERCOT) and in MISO's territory reflects both regional electricity demand and the land availability these operators serve.

On the pricing side, commercial electricity rates—the closest available proxy for data center power costs—range from $8.66 per megawatt-hour in Texas to $27.33 per megawatt-hour in California as of June 2026, a spread that will likely influence data center siting decisions as interconnection delays push projects forward. The 54,798 megawatt-hours of commercial sales reported in June show Texas consuming 15,754 MWh at the lowest rate, while California consumed 10,025 MWh at nearly triple the price; this divergence matters because interconnection timelines and local electricity costs directly determine where new computing infrastructure becomes economically viable. Watch whether MISO's 3,846-project queue—the largest by request count—begins moving through early stages faster than ERCOT's backlog, since MISO territory offers better price parity with Texas while serving the upper Midwest's emerging data center clusters.
